content.text: reg fluid balance and n./muscle function
Primary intracellular cation; critical for cardiac and muscle function
↑ (hyperkalemia): renal failure, acidosis, ACE inhibitor use
Main extracellular anion; works with sodium to maintain fluid and acid-base balance
Reflects body's buffering capacity; main component of acid-base balance
↑: metabolic alkalosis (vomiting, diuretics, excessive antacid use)
↓: metabolic acidosis (DKA, renal failure, lactic acidosis)
Waste product of protein metabolism, cleared by kidneys
↑: dehydration, renal failure, ↑protein intake, GI bleed, muscle breakdown
↑: acute kidney injury, chronic kidney dz, rhabdomyolysis
↓: low muscle mass, preg, liver dz
Ratio used to differentiate pre-renal vs intrinsic renal causes
<10: intrinsic renal dz, malnutrition, liver failure
Blood sugar level; reg by insulin & glucagon
↓ (hypoglycemia): insulin excess, adrenal insufficiency, liver failure
Regulated by PTH and vit D
essential for bone health, clotting, ♡ function
↑ (hypercalcemia): hyperparathyroidism, malig, vit D toxicity (confusion, stones)
↓ (hypocalcemia): hypoparathyroidism, vit D deficiency, pancreatitis (tetany, sz)
low levels allow fluid to leak into tissues
↓ albumin: malnutrition, liver dz, nephrotic syndrome, chronic illness
Enzymes released when liver or muscle cells are damaged
Marked ↑: viral hepatitis, drug-induced liver injury, ischemic hepatitis
AST > ALT ratio suggests alcoholic hepatitis
Enzyme from liver, bone, bile ducts
elevated in cholestatic liver dz and bone dx
↑: cholestasis, Paget's disease, bone metastases, primary biliary cholangitis
Isolated ALP elevation w norm transaminases suggests bone or bile duct origin
